sum: A short out-and-back trek from the Juphal airstrip up the Suligad gorge to Phoksundo Lake at 3,612 m, staying in simple lodges and needing a Lower Dolpo permit.

guide.note: Lower Dolpo is a restricted area, so the permit comes only through a registered trekking agency and you must walk with a licensed guide, whether you are alone or in a group. On the ground, a guide who knows the lodge owners makes the difference between a bed and a meal and a locked door, especially in the yarsagumba season when many families are away.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj on the plains near the Indian border, spend the night, and take the early flight to Juphal in Dolpa next morning. Juphal flights run only in calm, clear weather, so a delay of a day or more at either end is common. A rough road now links Dunai with the lowlands, but it is slow and often blocked.

photo.a: The turquoise Phoksundo Lake fills a deep basin between steep rock slopes streaked with snow, seen from a forested hillside high above the water.
photo.c: Phoksundo Lake in Shey Phoksundo National Park, Dolpo

includes: Shey Phoksundo park permit and Lower Dolpo permit
lodge or tent nights and three meals a day on the trek

permits.name: Shey Phoksundo National Park entry permit
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or the park entry post on the trail in from Juphal.

permits.name: Lower Dolpo restricted area permit
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week, then USD 5 a day

fees.per: person per week, then USD 5 a day

permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

transportText: Flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj and on to Juphal, and the same back
tips: Take all your cash from Kathmandu or Nepalgunj. Do not count on finding a working cash machine in Dolpa.
Lodges are simple rooms around a kitchen fire. Bring a sleeping bag, and expect dal bhat, noodles, potatoes and Tibetan bread rather than a menu.
Nepalgunj is hot for most of the year; pack one set of light clothes for the night there.
Walk round Bon shrines and mani walls anticlockwise, the opposite of Buddhist custom, and ask before taking photographs inside Tshowa monastery.
Water in the gorge comes from the river and from side streams used by livestock. Treat all of it.

days.t: Fly to Juphal, walk to Dunai
days.note: After the dawn flight from Nepalgunj, walk down through Juphal's terraces to the Thuli Bheri and follow the valley road upstream to the district town, where your permit is registered. Jeeps cover the same stretch if you would rather ride.

Cross the river, walk downstream to the national park gate where the Suligad joins, and turn north into the gorge. The trail climbs and drops beside the water through walnut and pine past Kageni and Shyanta. Permits are checked at the gate.

A long day of short, steep ups and downs beside the river, crossing it on log and suspension bridges. Above Rechi the valley divides at Sumduwa, where the park has its headquarters; the lodges at Chunuwar are a little beyond.

days.t: Chunuwar to Ringmo and Phoksundo Lake
days.note: Climb steadily through Palam, the winter settlement of Ringmo's families, to a ridge with the first sight of the waterfall and, beyond it, the lake. An easy descent through birch brings you to Ringmo, a few minutes from the shore.

days.t: Day at Ringmo and Phoksundo Lake
days.note: Walk round the shore to Tshowa, the Bon monastery on a bluff above the water, then follow the Upper Dolpo trail up the western cliffs for the classic view down the lake. The path is narrow with a long drop; turn back where it stops feeling comfortable.
Two stages of the walk in combined into one mostly downhill day, after a short climb back to the waterfall ridge. Leave early; it is a long way and the gorge is dark by late afternoon.
Down the last of the gorge to the park gate, then west along the Thuli Bheri and up the final 400 m to the airstrip village, the hottest climb of the trek. Reconfirm your seat as soon as you arrive.
Flights leave soon after sunrise while the air is still. A same-day connection to Kathmandu is usually possible, but keep a spare day before any international flight.
